stem: A ketamine prescription is presented to a Massachusetts community pharmacy. Which statements must be considered? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Ketamine is Schedule II and cannot be refilled.
Massachusetts treats ketamine as Schedule VI.
Schedule III refill limits apply to authorized refills.
Covered outpatient dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
Its anesthetic indication does not change Schedule III status.

explanation.core_reasoning: The supported conclusions on these facts are: Schedule III refill limits apply to authorized refills. Covered outpatient dispensing is reportable to MassPAT. Its anesthetic indication does not change Schedule III status.

choice_analysis.A: Not supported: Ketamine is Schedule II and cannot be refilled.
choice_analysis.B: Not supported: Massachusetts treats ketamine as Schedule VI.
choice_analysis.C: Supported: Schedule III refill limits apply to authorized refills.
choice_analysis.D: Supported: Covered outpatient dispensing is reportable to MassPAT.
choice_analysis.E: Supported: Its anesthetic indication does not change Schedule III status.

related_facts: ketamine (Ketalar) is used for induction and maintenance of general anesthesia; it is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.

Covered pharmacies report dispensing of Schedule II through V controlled substances and DPH-designated additional drugs, including gabapentin, to the Massachusetts PMP under the current submission standard.
explanation.mpje_trap: Distinguish this near-miss from the controlling rule: 'Ketamine is Schedule II and cannot be refilled.'

reasoning_steps: Classify ketamine under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
Match the scenario's operative facts to Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits
